question: When comparing two sewer basins of different sizes, what is the most useful first step before ranking their inflow and infiltration performance?
correctAnswer: Normalize flow by basin size, such as flow per hectare or per kilometre of pipe
explanation: Normalizing by size makes basins comparable, because a larger basin will usually carry more total flow even with similar leakage per unit area.
options: Normalize flow by basin size, such as flow per hectare or per kilometre of pipe
Compare only the total peak flow in each basin
Rank basins by the age of the oldest pipe only
Rank basins by the number of complaints received
optionA: Normalize flow by basin size, such as flow per hectare or per kilometre of pipe
optionB: Compare only the total peak flow in each basin
optionC: Rank basins by the age of the oldest pipe only
optionD: Rank basins by the number of complaints received
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: Basin A shows high night flow per hectare and Basin B shows high wet weather peaking only. What does this pattern most likely suggest?
correctAnswer: Basin A has more steady infiltration and Basin B has more rainfall dependent inflow
explanation: Steady night flow points to groundwater infiltration, while a wet weather peak points to rainfall dependent inflow from direct or indirect storm sources.
options: Both basins have identical sources that need no further checks
Basin A has more steady infiltration and Basin B has more rainfall dependent inflow
Basin A has only direct storm connections and Basin B has only groundwater leakage
Neither pattern is related to inflow and infiltration work
optionA: Both basins have identical sources that need no further checks
optionB: Basin A has more steady infiltration and Basin B has more rainfall dependent inflow
optionC: Basin A has only direct storm connections and Basin B has only groundwater leakage
optionD: Neither pattern is related to inflow and infiltration work

Stop flow monitoring in all other basins

Cancel monitoring because the normalized rates match

explanation: Step testing measures flow at successive points, usually at night, so a jump between points locates the section contributing the most infiltration.
